lawyer:
Abdus Salam Mondal DAG with Dipayan Saha, AAG ------ For the Defendant-Appellants. 
ABM Waliur Rahman Khan with Khalilur Rahman, Advocates ------ For the Plaintiffs-Respondents.
parties:
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ------ Defendants-Appellants
Vs
Amena Khatun and others ------ Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
ANM Bashir Ullah J: This First Appeal at the instance of the defendant-appellants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 30-6-2004 and 10-7-2004 respectively passed by the Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 30 of 2003 decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiffs-respondent Nos. 1-10.

2. The facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, in short, are that Md Meser Uddin filed Title Suit No. 1 of 1998 for declaration of his title along with confirmation of possession into the suit land. During the pendency of the suit he died, accordingly his legal heirs were substituted. Subsequently it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 82 of 2000 and lastly as 30 of 2003.

3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that 0.09 acres of land appertains to CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 12/87 of CS khatian Nos. 38 and 39 originally belonged to Sebesawor Das who settled the said land in favour of Sashi Kanto Dutta by a registered patta deed on 23rd Falgun, 1310 BS Sashi Kanta Dutta also settled the land in favour of Krishna Mohan Das and others by a registered patta on 11th jaista 1312 BS Krishna Mohan Das transferred the land by a registered kabala in favour of Gobinda Chandra Roy Chowdhury on 11th Vhadra, 1312 BS. The heirs of Gobinda Chandra Roy Chowdhury transferred the land by a kabala on 12th Boishakh, 1323 BS in favour of Bhabu Mohendra Chandra Dhar.

4. Babu Mohendra Chandra Dhar died leaving 5 sons. Surendra Chandra Dhar and others, the sons of Babu Mohendra Chandra Dhar transferred the land by a kabala dated 21-5-1939 in favour of Usa Rani Ghosh and Bijoy Hori Ghosh. Bijoy Hon Basu died leaving 2 sons Sudhir Ranjan Bosu and Subash Ranjan Bosu. Sudhir Ranjan Boshu as power of attorney of Usa Rani Gosh and Subash Ranjan Bosu and also on his behalf settled the land to one Abdul Karim Karwada by a registered deed dated 10-10-1952.

5. In the said instrument dated 10-10-1952 among other it was stated that the measurement of the land is 85' x 49' along with 21/2 passage in eastern side for sweeper. In the SA records of right the said land was recorded in the name of Abdul Karim Karwada. Abdul Karim Karwada gifted the said land through a heba deed to one Abdul Rouf Baburchi on 18-2-1960. Abdul Rouf sold the said land to one Kazi Serajul Islam by a kabala dated 10-4-1963. Kazi Serajul Islam sold the land to Meser Uddin, the original plaintiff (predecessor of the substituted plaintiffs) by a kabala dated 27-4-1964.

6. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Meser Uddin being the owner and possessor of the suit land paid rents to the government and constructed a 4 storied building on the suit land to live therein. The plaintiffs through amendment of the plaint claimed that from the very beginning Sebeswaor Das upto the last. kabala in favour of the plaintiffs Meser Uddin, the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12, 12/87 though were repeatedly in corporate in the instruments of transfer but in fact the suit land covered the CS and SA plot No. 12/87 corresponding to RS plot No. 75 of RS khatian No. 80 having an area of 0.05 acres of land and the same was recorded in the name of Profullah Roy Choudhury in the RS records of right. It is also averred in the plaint that when the plaintiffs approached the defendant No. 3 for taking the land development tax of 1402-1404 BS the defendant No. 3 declined to take the same from the plaintiffs for the wrong records of right. Thus the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of his title and confirmation of his possession.

7. The defendant No. 3 filing two written statements and additional written statement contested the suit. The statements of both the written statements are all most same and identical. The defendant in the written statement stated among others that the case is not maintainable in its present form and the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest into the suit land.

8. The case of the defendant, in short, is that 0.12 acres of land appertains to SA plot No. 12/88 corresponding to RS plot Nos. 75 and 76 of RS khatian Nos. 80 and 125 originally belonged to Non-bengali Abdul Halim and Harun. The suit land has been declared as abandoned property under President Order No. 16/72 and on the said land in one portion there are Sadar Thana land office, DB Police Office and in other parts different persons have been living taking lease from the government. Since the suit land is abandoned property, the present suit of the plaintiffs is not maintainable.

9. It is also stated in the written statement that the plaintiffs did not purchase the land of plot No. 12/88 from its real owner. Since the plaintiffs were not in a possession of the said land in SA and RS operation their names have not been recorded. The plaintiffs have introduced a fictitious boundary in order to grab the suit land. So, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs.

10. The trial Court upon the above pleadings framed as many as 5 issues to dispose of the suit and at trial the plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses while the defendant examined 1 witness and the plaintiffs filed some documents which were marked as exhibits 1-8(ka) while the defendant filed certified copy of RS khatian No. 125 only marked as exhibit A and A(1).

11. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence and other materials on record decreed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree. The defendant-appellants being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree of the trial Court preferred this appeal in this Court.

12. At the time of hearing of this appeal Mr Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mr Dipayan Saha, the learned Assistant Attorney-General taking us through the plaint, written statements, issues, both oral and documentary evidence and the memo of appeal supporting the appeal and assailing the judgment of the trial Court submits that the trial Court erred both in law and facts in decreeing the suit, the trial Court did not at all consider that the plaintiffs could not prove their title into the CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 or 12/88, the trial Court did not at all consider that at any stage of the records of right neither the name of the plaintiffs nor his predecessor were recorded, the trial Court did not at all consider that the suit land is in the possession of the defendants.

13. The learned Deputy Attorney-General also submits that since the plaintiffs could not show any document in support of the land which they allegedly purchased, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any decree for the suit land and the trial Court should have dismissed the suit. So, this Court should interfere in the judgment and decree, appealed against.

14. On the other hand, Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr ABM Waliur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondents supporting the judgment of the trial Court submits that it is fact that in all the deeds related to the suit land starting from the transfer Sebeswaor Das to Sashi Kanto Dutta the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 were incorporated in the instruments but during pendency of the suit a local investigation was held into the suit land when the Advocate Commissioner found that within the boundary given by the plaintiffs the land of CS plot No. 12/87 corresponding to RS plot No. 75 attract to the suit land and accordingly the plaint was amended to that effect.

15. The learned Advocate also submits that if it is conceded for a moment that the plaintiffs had entered into the possession on the basis of some erroneous or invalid title deeds but since their possession has been proved for the long time starting from 1310 BS till filing of the suit, the plaintiffs have acquired indefeasible title into the suit land.

16. The learned Advocate also further submits that it is in the evidence of the defendant's witness that the DB Police Office and the AC (Land) office are situated in RS plot No. 76 but the plaintiff's clear case is that their suit land attract the RS plot No. 75 of RS kahtian No. 80 but the RS plot No. 75 will go to show that only 0.05 acres of land have been recorded in R5 plot No. 75. Although the plaintiffs are in possession of 0.09 acres of land but whenever there will be a conflict between the area of land mentioned in the plot number and the land found within the given boundary physically, the area of land found within the boundary will prevail and in support of his such contention the learned Advocate of the respondents referred the case of Md Alkas Ali Khan vs Monsur Ahmed Khan 1983 BLD (AD) 126.

17. The learned Advocate also submits that in the written statements among others it was averred that the suit land has been declared as abandoned property under President Order No. 16 of 1972 but the defendants at trial could not show papers that the suit land was listed in the gazette notification under Ordinance 54 of 1985. So, the oral claim as to the abandoned property of the suit land is not sufficient to hold that the suit land was declared as abandoned property at any point of time. The learned Advocate for the respondents in support of his such contention referred the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Mir Md Imam Hossain 2 AIR (AD) 47.

18. The learned Advocate in his concluding submissions submits that there is no denial of the fact that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land having a 4 storied building thereon and there is no case in the hands of the defendant-appellants that anybody else other than the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. So, the trial Court considering all these facts and materials on record rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and since there appears no error or law and facts in the judgment of the trial Court, the same may kindly be upheld.

19. We have considered the above arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record particularly the plaint, written statements, evidence on record, the judgment pronounced by the trial Court and the appeal filed by the defendant-appellants.

20. In order to appreciate the arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties let us have a look into the evidence on record. As we have noticed it earlier that the plaintiffs examined 5 witnesses at trial of them PW 1 Md Osman Gani, who is the plaintiff No. 2 stated that they have been possessing 0.09 acres of land which has been recorded in RS plot No. 75 of RS khatian No. 80, there is a road in the north of their suit land, in the south a filled up tank, in the east the building of Mr Harun where there is an office of defendant No. 2 and in the west Shamsuddin Ahmed and others.

21. He further stated that the arms of the suit land in the east-west side is 85 feet and in the north south side 49 feet having a passage of 2½' x 49' in its east side.

22. He also stated that while Gobinda Chandra Roy Choudhury was owner and possessor of the suit land transferred the same in favour of Mahendra Chandra Dhar. The 5 sons of Mahendra Chandra Dhar namely Surendra and others sold the suit land to Usa Rani in 1939, Sudhir Ranjan Basu on his behalf and also as power of attorney of Usa Rani and Suvas Ranjan Basu transferred the suit land in favour of Abdul Karim in 1952, Abdul Karim transferred the suit land to Abdur Rouf on 18-12-1960 and possession was delivered to Abdur Rouf, Abdul Rouf sold the suit land by a kabala dated 10-4-1963 in favour of Sirajul Islam and Sirajul Islam sold the land to their predecessor Md Meser Uddin on 27-11-1964, his father constructed a building on the suit land and paid land development taxes upto 1401 BS but declined to take rents for the years 1402-1404 BS.

23. He also stated that in RS plot No. 75 though 0.05 acres of land has been recorded but within their given boundary there is 0.09 acres of land which also attract the CS and SA plot Nos. 12/88 and 12/89. He also stated that they did not possess the land of RS plot No. 76. PW 1 proved the deed in favour of Abdur Rouf by Abdul Karim Karwada marked as Exhibit-1, the sale deed in favour of Kazi Sirajul Islam by Kazi Abdul Rouf dated 10-4-1963 marked as Exhibit-2 and also sale deed in favour of Meser Uddin by Kazi Sirajul Islam on 27-11-1964 marked as Exhibit-3. He also filed the certified copy of RS khatian No. 80, marked Exhibit 5 and CS khatian No. 38 marked Exhibit 5(ka).

24. In cross-examination of the defendants he denied the defendants suggestion that they are not in the possession in RS plot No. 75. He also denied the further defendants suggestion that their suit land did not cover the land of RS plot No. 75.

25. PW 2 Gopal Chandra Das stated that he is a Staff Moharar of Registration Complex, Tejgaon, Dhaka. He further stated that perpetual lease deed No. 561 dated 17-1-1953 has been registered in volum No. 253 at page Nos. 172-177. The certified copy of the lease deed in favour of Abdul Karim Karwada has been marked as Exhibit 6. There is no significant cross-examination of this PW 2. In the aid deed Usa Rani Das and others appear as the 1st party.

26. PW 3 Md Habib Ullah stated that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land from 1965 and before the plaintiffs All Kazi, Sirajul Islam and Abdul Rouf used to possess the suit land and before them. Abdul Karim Karwadi used to possess the suit land. In cross-examination PW 3 stated that he has no house at Narayanganj but in 1380 BS he used to live at Chashara, Karim Karwada was known to him from 1963-64.

27. PW 4 AKM Bodiruzzaman stated that the heirs of Meser Ali have been possessing the suit land and Meser Ali had purchased the land in 1964 who got the same from Karim Karwada. In cross-examination he stated that he has house at Narayanganj.

28. PW 5 Md Giasuddin, a Survey knowing Advocate Commissioner stated that he held a commission as per direction for the Court and submitted his report on 10-7-2002 in the Court. He proved the local investigation report marked Exhibit 7 and his signature in it marked exhibit 7(ka). In cross-examination he stated that he had related the CS and RS map, he took a fixed station in the west corner of plot No. 12/87 since there was a pillar. He also stated that the suit land covered the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS plot No. 12/88 and the land of RS plot No. 76 is situated just east of the land of RS plot No. 75 and in the land of RS plot No. 76 there are CID Police Office and AC (Land) office also.

29. The defendant examined 1 witness Md Abdur Rahman who in his testimony stated that he has been serving as a Land Assistant Officer. He also stated that the suit land has been recorded in SA plot No. 12/88 corresponding to RS plot Nos. 75 and 76. The RS plot No. 76 has been recorded in the name of the government as abandoned property while the land of RS plot No. 75 has been recorded in the name of Profulla and others. At the time of preparation of RS records of right, the plaintiffs were not in possession into the suit land and the plaintiffs did not raise their voice against RS records of right. In the suit land there are some government establishment like Union Vumi Office, CID office and Staffs quarters. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land. The DW 1 filed the certified copy of Rs khatian Nos. 125 and 80 marked exhibits A and A(1).

30. In cross-examination DW 1 stated that the RS plot No. 75 corresponds to SA plot No. 12/88 the land of RS plot No. 76 is the government land, the area of RS plot No. 75 is 0.05 acres. He denied the suggestion that RS plot No. 75 is covered by an area of. 0.09 acres of land.

31. These are the evidences that have been given by the plaintiffs and the defendants in the suit. It is almost admitted in the suit that though all the kabalas mentioned in the plaint were for the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 9, 10, 12 and 12/87 but after filing of the suit the plaintiffs amended the plaint claiming the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88 and those plot numbers were very much absent in the deeds mentioned in the plaint.

32. A local investigation was held in to the suit land by PW 5 who in his cross-examination stated that the lands found within the given boundary by the plaintiffs in the plaint covers the land of RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88. The Advocate Commissioner's report shows the area of the land within the given boundary covers as .09 acres of land. The RS khatian No. 80 is going to show that RS plot No. 75 appears to have .05 acres of land.

33. The plaintiffs in order to prove their possession into the suit land examined PWs 1, 3 and 4. PW 1 stated that his father purchased the land from Sirajul Islam in 1964 and from then they are in possession into the suit land and his father constructed a building into the suit land to live therein. His such evidence is being strongly corroborated by the evidence of PWs 3 and 4. PWs 3 and 4 were cross-examined extensively by the defendants but there is nothing in their testimonies for which we can disbelieve their evidence as to the possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land.

34. There is also strong hint in the evidence of DW 1 regarding the possession of the plaintiffs. DW 1 in his evidence stated that the land of CS and SA plot No. 12/88 has been recorded in RS plot Nos. 75 and 76. He also stated that the land of RS plot No. 76 is the government property. There is no case either, in the written statement or in the evidence of DW 1 that the land of RS plot No. 75 was purchased and possessed by any other person other than the plaintiffs.

35. The trial Court on the right assessment of the evidence of PWs 1, 3 and 4 and DW 1 rightly found the uninterrupted possession of the plaintiffs into the suit land from 1964 till the filing of the suit in the year 1998. Though the correct RS plot No. 75 corresponding to CS and SA plot No. 12/88 were not mentioned in the purchase deed of Meser Ali dated 27-4-1964 but on the basis of the said wrong or invalid instrument Meser Ali had been into the possession of the suit land and he maintained his such possession till now. As such we are of the view that though the plaintiffs had entered into the possession of the suit land on the basis of invalid transfer deed but the plaintiffs have acquired good title for his long possession which is in all counts more than 12 years and our such views are strongly supported by the decisions of the cases of 1 MLR (AD) 71, 54 DLR (AD) 173 and also 17 BLD 251 = 1 BLC 183.

36. It is the case of the plaintiffs that though the suit land has been recorded wrongly in RS plot No. 75 showing an area of 0.05 acres but in fact within the given boundary as appended in the deed of the plaintiffs of 1964 (Exhibit 2(ka) covers an area of 0.09 acre of land. This case of the plaintiffs has been supported by the Advocate Commissioner's report. PW 5 in his evidence testified that he held the local investigation into the suit land and filed a report on completion of the investigation. The report shows that he found 0.09 acres of land within the given boundary.

<u>37. In this case the learned Advocate for the respondents referring the case of 1983 BLD (AD) 126 submits that when there is conflict between the area of plot mentioned there and the area within the boundary of the instrument, the area within the boundary of instrument shall prevail over the area of the plot mentioned. We have gone through the reported case of Md Alkas Ali vs Mansur Ahmed Khan 1983 BLD (AD) 126. In the reported case it was held that conflict between the area of the plot mentioned in the plot Nos. and within the boundary, the area within the boundary shall prevail. As such we are of the view that though in RS plot No. 75 only 0.05 acres of land has been recorded in the name of others but the plaintiff's possession have been found in the RS plot No. 75 and in the local investigation an area of 0.09 acres of land has also been found within the given boundary of the plaint. So, we are of the view that the area of the land found within the given boundary by the Advocate Commissioner will prevail upon RS plot No. 75 of RS khatin No. 80.</u>

38. As such having regards to the above discussion and also going through all the relevant documents connected with the suit we are of the view that the trial Court did not commit any error of law and fact in coming to the conclusion to find the title of the plaintiffs into 0.09 acres of land which the plaintiffs have been possessing from 1964. So we find it difficult to discover any error of fact or law in the judgment passed by the trial Court.

39. In the result, the appeal is dismissed. However there is no order as to costs.

Let a copy of this judgment and order be communicated to the Court concerned with the lower Court's record at once.

End.
